fullText.simplified:
第七章、危险的秦国使者

    当我在云梦泽难过时，秦国派了使者来引都。这位使者叫张宜。
    张宜对楚怀王说：“只要楚国与齐国断交，秦国就把商屋的六百里地还给楚国。”
    还记得商屋吗？我在前面介绍楚国时说过，商屋原来是楚国非常重要的一块土地，但后来被秦国抢去了，楚国的王一直想把它要回来。
    楚怀王心动了，同意了秦国的要求。他马上和齐国断交，并派人跟张宜去秦国收回土地。但没想到，楚国的人刚到秦国，张宜就说自己病了，然后关门不见客了。
    直到一个多月后，张宜才重新出现，但他说：“我答应给楚怀王的是六里地，不是六百里地，我从来没有说过六百里。”
    这么重要的事情，张宜居然骗人！楚怀王生气极了，决定派军队去攻打秦国。
    我听到这些消息，马上回引都去见楚怀王。战争需要好好计划，着急地把军队送去战场，可能不会有好结果。但我还没到引都，军队就已经出发了。我跑去军队会经过的一个路口，在那儿见到了正向秦国走去的军队。
    “不要去！再想一想，想好了再做决定！战争不是最好的解决办法！”我大声叫。很多人都听到了，但没有人停下脚步。我一直叫，声音也变了，后来再也发不出声音了。
    我望着走远的军队，眼泪掉了下来。
    战争在楚国一个叫单阳的地方开始了。秦军很厉害，楚军死了很多人。
    没有人来帮楚国。楚怀王轻易决定与齐国断交的事情，让齐王很生气，他当然不会来帮忙。另外四个小国就更不用说了，他们不但不帮忙，其中两个小国还抓住机会，一起出兵攻打楚国的东北方，抢走了楚国的一座城。
    最后，楚军败了，八万人战死，单阳也被秦国抢走了。听到这些消息，我既心痛，又生气。我为那些死在前方的楚国士兵心痛，也为楚国失去的土地心痛。
    这时，王宫来人了，楚怀王要见我。
fullText.traditional:
第七章、危險的秦國使者

    當我在雲夢澤難過時，秦國派了使者來引都。這位使者叫張宜。
    張宜對楚懷王說：“只要楚國與齊國斷交，秦國就把商屋的六百里地還給楚國。”
    還記得商屋嗎？我在前面介紹楚國時說過，商屋原來是楚國非常重要的一塊土地，但後來被秦國搶去了，楚國的王一直想把它要回來。
    楚懷王心動了，同意了秦國的要求。他馬上和齊國斷交，並派人跟張宜去秦國收回土地。但沒想到，楚國的人剛到秦國，張宜就說自己病了，然後關門不見客了。
    直到一個多月後，張宜才重新出現，但他說：“我答應給楚懷王的是六里地，不是六百里地，我從來沒有說過六百里。”
    這麼重要的事情，張宜居然騙人！楚懷王生氣極了，決定派軍隊去攻打秦國。
    我聽到這些消息，馬上回引都去見楚懷王。戰爭需要好好計劃，著急地把軍隊送去戰場，可能不會有好結果。但我還沒到引都，軍隊就已經出發了。我跑去軍隊會經過的一個路口，在那兒見到了正向秦國走去的軍隊。
    “不要去！再想一想，想好了再做決定！戰爭不是最好的解決辦法！”我大聲叫。很多人都聽到了，但沒有人停下腳步。我一直叫，聲音也變了，後來再也發不出聲音了。
    我望著走遠的軍隊，眼淚掉了下來。
    戰爭在楚國一個叫丹陽的地方開始了。秦軍很厲害，楚軍死了很多人。
    沒有人來幫楚國。楚懷王輕易決定與齊國斷交的事情，讓齊王很生氣，他當然不會來幫忙。另外四個小國就更不用說了，他們不但不幫忙，其中兩個小國還抓住機會，一起出兵攻打楚國的東北方，搶走了楚國的一座城。
    最後，楚軍敗了，八萬人戰死，丹陽也被秦國搶走了。聽到這些消息，我既心痛，又生氣。我為那些死在前方的楚國士兵心痛，也為楚國失去的土地心痛。
    這時，王宮來人了，楚懷王要見我。

sentences.traditional: 戰爭需要好好計劃，著急地把軍隊送去戰場，可能不會有好結果。

sentences.pinyin: dàn wǒ hái méi dào yǐn dū jūn duì jiù yǐ jīng chū fā le

sentences.english: “Don’t go! Think it over before making a decision! War is not the best solution!” I shouted loudly.

sentences.english: Many people heard me, but no one stopped. I kept shouting until my voice changed, and eventually,  I could no longer make a sound.

sentences.simplified: 我望着走远的军队，眼泪掉了下来。

sentences.english: I watched the army march away, tears falling from my eyes.

sentences.simplified: 战争在楚国一个叫单阳的地方开始了。秦军很厉害，楚军死了很多人。
sentences.traditional: 戰爭在楚國一個叫丹陽的地方開始了。秦軍很厲害，楚軍死了很多人。

sentences.english: The war began in a place called Danyang in the state of Chu. The Qin army was formidable, and many Chu soldiers died.

sentences.simplified: 没有人来帮楚国。
sentences.traditional: 沒有人來幫楚國。
sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu rén lái bāng chǔ guó
sentences.english: No one came to help Chu.

sentences.simplified: 楚怀王轻易决定与齐国断交的事情，让齐王很生气，他当然不会来帮忙。
sentences.traditional: 楚懷王輕易決定與齊國斷交的事情，讓齊王很生氣，他當然不會來幫忙。

sentences.english: King Huai of Chu had rashly decided to sever ties with the state of Qi. This angered the King of Qi, so he certainly wouldn’t come to help.

sentences.traditional: 另外四個小國就更不用說了，

sentences.english: As for the other four small states, it goes without saying.

sentences.english: Not only did they not assist, but two of them seized the opportunity to send troops to attack Chu’s northeastern border, capturing a city.

sentences.simplified: 最后，楚军败了，八万人战死，单阳也被秦国抢走了。
sentences.traditional: 最後，楚軍敗了，八萬人戰死，丹陽也被秦國搶走了。

sentences.english: In the end, the Chu army was defeated, with eighty thousand soldiers killed in battle. Danyang was also taken by Qin.

sentences.simplified: 听到这些消息，我既心痛，又生气。
sentences.traditional: 聽到這些消息，我既心痛，又生氣。
sentences.pinyin: tīng dào zhè xiē xiāo xi wǒ jì xīn tòng yòu shēng qì
sentences.english: Hearing this news, I felt both heartbroken and angry.

sentences.traditional: 我為那些死在前方的楚國士兵心痛，也為楚國失去的土地心痛。

sentences.english: I was heartbroken for the Chu soldiers who died on the front lines and for the land that Chu lost.

sentences.simplified: 这时，王宫来人了，楚怀王要见我。
sentences.traditional: 這時，王宮來人了，楚懷王要見我。

sentences.english: At this moment, someone from the royal palace came, saying that King Huai of Chu wanted to see me.

sentence_translations: Chapter 7: The Dangerous Envoy from Qin
While I was in Yunmeng Lakes feeling sad, the state of Qin sent an envoy to Yindu. This envoy was named Zhang Yi.
Zhang Yi said to King Huai of Chu, “As long as Chu breaks off relations with Qi, Qin will return the six hundred li of Shangwu to Chu.”
Do you remember Shangwu?
As I mentioned earlier when introducing the state of Chu, Shangwu was originally a very important piece of land belonging to Chu.
But later, it was seized by Qin, and the kings of Chu had always wanted to win it back.
King Huai of Chu was tempted and agreed to Qin’s request.
He immediately broke off relations with Qi and sent people with Zhang Yi to Qin to reclaim the land.
But unexpectedly, as soon as the people from Chu arrived in Qin, Zhang Yi claimed he was ill and then shut his doors to visitors.
It wasn’t until over one month later that Zhang Yi reappeared, but he said, ..
.. “What I promised King Huai of Chu was six li of land, not six hundred li of land. I never said six hundred li.”
Zhang Yi had, shockingly, deceived them on such an important matter!
King Huai of Chu was extremely angry and decided to send troops to attack Qin.
When I heard this news, I immediately returned to Yindu to see King Huai of Chu.
War needs careful planning, and hastily sending troops to the battlefield might not yield good results.
But the troops had already set out before I had reached Yindu.
I ran to a crossroads where the army would pass, and there I saw the troops heading toward Qin.
“Don’t go! Think it over before making a decision! War is not the best solution!” I shouted loudly.
Many people heard me, but no one stopped. I kept shouting until my voice changed, and eventually,  I could no longer make a sound.
I watched the army march away, tears falling from my eyes.
The war began in a place called Danyang in the state of Chu. The Qin army was formidable, and many Chu soldiers died.
No one came to help Chu.
King Huai of Chu had rashly decided to sever ties with the state of Qi. This angered the King of Qi, so he certainly wouldn’t come to help.
As for the other four small states, it goes without saying.
Not only did they not assist, but two of them seized the opportunity to send troops to attack Chu’s northeastern border, capturing a city.
In the end, the Chu army was defeated, with eighty thousand soldiers killed in battle. Danyang was also taken by Qin.
Hearing this news, I felt both heartbroken and angry.
I was heartbroken for the Chu soldiers who died on the front lines and for the land that Chu lost.
At this moment, someone from the royal palace came, saying that King Huai of Chu wanted to see me.
